reading: The BBC asked people how the government's new money plans affect their lives.
Dave Herbert works as a driver.
He spends about £350 a month on petrol for work and his own trips.
Dave wanted a lower tax on fuel, but the government did not lower it.
A 19-year-old woman is looking for work.
She wants businesses to get more money so they can give jobs to more young people.
Robert Portlock lives with his parents and wants to move out.
He says rent for a small flat would take most of his monthly pay.
Chloe lives with her son and pays about £200 a month for gas and electricity.
She tries to spend no more than £40 a week on food.
She thinks the government's £100 energy payment will help her.

vocabulary.definition: A liquid that many cars use to run.
To leave your home and start living somewhere else.
Money you pay to live in a home that belongs to someone else.
To use money to pay for something.

entries.ja: 多くの車が走るために使う液体。

entries.de: Eine Flüssigkeit, die viele Autos zum Fahren verwenden.
